# Derived MIT code

Source: PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet 0.3.7 (npm baseline retained in compat/dsh-pet-0.3.7/manifest.json).
`player.js` derives its loader from the reviewed `switchPresentationVideo` patch, with a small lifecycle wrapper and own namespace. The current candidate keeps both decoding videos hidden and presents one attached Canvas2D surface. Each decoded frame is drawn into a detached canvas first, then replaces the whole visible bitmap with the `copy` operation. The previous painter remains active while a replacement loads; ownership changes only after a successful copy. Cancellation, timeout and disposal fence late callbacks. Visible playback never clears or resizes an already populated surface. An ended incoming video without another drawable callback times out and preserves the old output.

This candidate requires Canvas2D and video-to-canvas drawing. It prefers `requestVideoFrameCallback`, with a cancellable animation-frame fallback. It performs no pixel readback/export and adds no CORS relaxation, Worker, OffscreenCanvas, dependency or runtime binary. At the silver source size of 640×360, the two RGBA canvas backings total about 1.76 MiB, excluding video decoders, GPU/compositor copies and other browser storage. Each presented frame adds a buffer draw and a full-surface copy. Actual VP9-alpha preservation, hidden-video callback cadence, CPU/GPU cost, screen continuity and visual quality remain subject to bounded native verification; unit pixel contracts do not establish that acceptance.

It excludes the original host, model services, menus, art, prompts, fonts, and network polling. `work-status.js` (when present) is generated from the MIT work-status reducer. Company changes and feedback modules remain covered by CODE-LICENSE.md. Upstream copyright and full MIT terms are in LICENSE. Artwork remains separately licensed and attributed under ASSET-LICENSE.md; this player change does not alter those terms.
